correctness.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING route verified as genuinely target-derived (wall-equation + scans + slice isolation per discovery_context), so audited on full standard with no presumption. Replayed: central-charge wall equation y=2(M*sv-N*sa)/(Q(Mr-N)) confirmed via derive_wall.py sympy output; spherical specialization and b^2 identity b^2=r*D2-2*CDOT+(v2+2S+2r-2) confirmed (b^2-expected=0). Slice (r=2,C=H,S=0,N=Q,S=0) den>0 same-phase emptiness proof is correct: Y>0 forces D2<=-2, M>Q/2, then b^2=2D2-2M+Q+2<-2 strictly; fuzz-tested on 500 random hyperbolic lattices/box-12 (30098 den>0 walls, 0 violations) plus logged 498/451/829-wall checks. Closed forms Y=(D2+2)/(Q-2M) and anti-phase ray Y=(k^2+1)/(2k+1), b^2=4k^2+4k+4 (Q=2) verified exactly. BUT two essential inferences fail as written: (i) the uniform bound derivation claims max over real 0<M<Q/2 of (M^2/Q+2)/(Q-2M) equals Q/4+2 — false; over reals the function diverges to +infinity as M->Q/2-. The conclusion Y<Q/4+2 is true only after using integrality (M,Q integers, Q even for K3 so Q-2M>=2; odd-lattice case >=1), which the draft never states. The stated calculus is wrong, not just terse. (ii) anti-phase 'never destabilizing' is asserted without the required heart-membership argument (Im Za=xM<0 so a cannot lie in the large-volume heart as subobject/quotient); closed forms are proved but the destabilization inference is not. Hence headline not fully proved as written.

originality.rationale: Live-retrieval contract executed: Exa general (no category restriction, numResults<=8/<=5) for literal slice statement, Bayer-Macri actual-vs-numerical schema, Maciocia bounds, Mukai-vector bound, and uniform-census dominance queries; structured auxiliaries scope-literature-search openalex+crossref for Bayer-Macri, Maciocia, and spherical-wall queries (20 each); direct arXiv fetches of 1202.4587 and 1301.6968 abstracts/history. Nearest priors: Bayer-Macri 1301.6968 (numerical wall schema via hyperbolic lattice, MMP; no effectivity inequality), Maciocia 1202.4587 (fixed-surface nested/bounded walls, C0/R0; no slice den>0 formula or B=Q/4+2), Bottini/Bridgeland/Yoshioka/Liu/Li-Liu-Ouchi (generic existence, Stab construction, rank-1 algorithm; disjoint). Failure modes tested (see decisive_checks): no synonymous/dual encoding, no broader theorem, no database table, and no prior implication states or implies the exact slice den>0 emptiness plus Y/B closed forms. The slice formulas are novel as stated, though elementary. Originality PASSES.

value.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING assessed under ordinary full value standard with no presumption. The surviving headline is a single Mukai-shape slice (r=2,C=H,S=0) two-line substitution into the standard wall + Mukai-square formulas: den>0 emptiness is immediate algebra, den<0 'candidates' are only b^2-passing (necessary, explicitly not sufficient, so no actual wall is established), and the anti-phase tail is a phase-ordering observation. This is a mere parameter substitution / textbook exercise relative to the admitted target (all v), with arbitrary scope (no pre-computation motivation for v=(2,H,0) as a distinguished moduli problem; discovery was scan-driven post hoc). The claimed 'machine-checkable pre-filter' adds nothing over directly computing b^2, has no named downstream user or theorem, and no census is completed. Honest falsifications (218 counterexamples, fallback counterexample) delimit scope but do not create independent retrieval value. A rigorously established narrow datum can pass, but only when the object/invariant was motivated before computation and a future researcher could need the precise fact; neither holds here, and certification alone does not rescue an arbitrary slice. Intrinsic low value / arbitrary scope => FAIL.
